findings.explanation: Splunkbase 4022 is 'Technical Addon for the Metricator application for Nmon (HEC)'. The Cisco ACI add-on was TA_cisco-ACI (1897), archived in favour of Cisco DC Networking (7777). The 4022 ID is repeated in detailedImplementation and references.
findings.suggested_fix: Use Cisco DC Networking (cisco_dc_networking_app_for_splunk, Splunkbase 7777) for APIC API collection, mention TA_cisco-ACI (1897) only as deprecated, and remove 4022.

findings.explanation: APIC fault lifecycle states are soaking, soaking-clearing, raised, raised-clearing and retaining. 'cleared' is a severity, and 'retained' is not a state. Readers who build filters on these literals will never match retaining faults.
findings.suggested_fix: List the documented lc values (soaking, soaking-clearing, raised, raised-clearing, retaining), and say that cleared is the severity a fault takes when it enters retaining.

findings.explanation: Cisco documents the soaking, clearing and retention intervals in the fault lifecycle profile `fault:LcP`, with a retention default of 3600 seconds (one hour), not about five days. faultRecord purging is governed by the fault record retention policy `fault:ARetP`, which is record-count based. The same wrong class and five-day figure appear in the hardware field.
findings.quote: Map **fault retention** defaults under `fvFaultLifecycleP` (~five-day **cleared** storage) versus **raise/clear soak** windows often **30–120s** clear-side; newer trains add `fvFaultLcP` per-code overrides
findings.suggested_fix: Replace fvFaultLifecycleP and fvFaultLcP with fault:LcP (soak 120 s, clear 120 s, retain 3600 s by default) and fault:ARetP for faultRecord retention.

findings.explanation: These percentages are presented as Cisco's health-score fault weights, but they look made up. Cisco's documented default health-score penalty weights differ.
findings.quote: `weight_band` echoes Cisco severity weights feeding composite scoring (**critical** **90%**, **major** **60%**, **minor** **30%**, **warning** **10%**
findings.suggested_fix: Check the ACI Fundamentals health-score chapter for the default fault-severity weights. Either quote them exactly or describe weight_band as a local heuristic.

findings.explanation: Two references ('Faults, Events, and System Messages Management Guide' and 'FaultInst API Reference') point at the cisco.com and developer.cisco.com home pages instead of the named documents.
findings.suggested_fix: Link the APIC Faults guide (https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/switches/datacenter/aci/apic/sw/all/faults/guide/b_APIC_Faults_Errors/b_IFC_Faults_Errors_chapter_01.html) and the faultInst page of the APIC MIM reference.

findings.explanation: faultCounts backlog gauges are not asset inventory records. The Inventory datamodel does not fit this fault-trend signal.
The end-of-support date for APIC 4.x is stated without a source, and Cisco's end-of-life milestones differ by 4.x maintenance release.
findings.quote: APIC clusters running 4.x or earlier (out of support since Mar 2024)
findings.suggested_fix: Check the Cisco EoL bulletin for APIC 4.2 and cite it, or drop the date.

findings.explanation: An automated agent reviewed the UC ('agent-handcraft-2026-04-29'), and it contains wrong lifecycle states, fault-code meanings and an add-on ID, so the verified status is not supported.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade status until an ACI SME signs off.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `retained_like` tests `lc_state IN ("cleared","retained")`, but the APIC lifecycle value is `retaining` (cleared is a severity), so retained faultInst rows are never counted and `avg_mttr_hint_sec` stays empty. `active_like` also leaves out `soaking-clearing`.

The mnemonic tags mislabel fault codes. F1394 is a fabric (leaf-to-spine) port down, cause interface-physical-down, rule ethpm-if-port-down-fabric, not 'tep_ip_change'. F0532 is a port down used by an EPG (ethpm-if-port-down-infra-epg), not 'port_deny_evt'. Check F0103, F0613, F0982 and F2102 against the APIC fault catalogue as well.

`strptime(created,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%3N")` drops the `+00:00` offset that APIC includes in created, ackTime and lastTransition, so timestamps are read in the search head's timezone and MTTA/MTTR can be skewed. Add `%:z` to the format.

summary: The UC explains the fault MO families (faultInst, faultDelegate, faultCounts, faultRecord) well, but several APIC facts are wrong. It uses invented lifecycle states ('cleared', 'retained' instead of 'retaining'), gives wrong meanings for fault codes F0532 and F1394, names a non-existent lifecycle policy class with the wrong retention default, and cites the wrong Splunkbase ID.
